source_span: While US 10-year nominal yields are up around 97bps so far this year, only around 10bps of that is due to higher breakevens. The remainder reflects significantly higher real yields, which are now at levels last seen in 2008.
source_chain: 10yr yields are up ~97bps this year but only ~10bps of that is breakevens (inflation expectations, stable 3+ years) and term premium is flat for 18 months (ruling out fiscal fear), therefore the move is almost entirely real yields, therefore it reflects policy rates and a higher neutral rate driven by growth strength (strong PMI, GDPNow, earnings) rather than inflation fear; boundary condition: Raskin's neutral-rate range is elevated but still plausible, with yields now edging toward its upper bound.
pulse_chain: The flash PMI beat sharply (58.4 vs 55.3 est, a five-year high) and triggered a bond selloff to post-2007/2008-level yields, therefore decomposing the ~97bps yield rise shows only ~10bps from breakevens (flat 3+ years) and a flat term premium (18 months), ruling out inflation and fiscal fear as drivers, therefore what's left is the policy-rate/neutral-rate path (hike odds rising, GS adding a second hike), with DB's Raskin view placing the neutral rate at the elevated-but-plausible upper bound now being tested.
why: The pulse reproduces DB's exact decomposition (97bps/10bps breakevens/3-year-stable/18-month-flat term premium) in the same direction and same non-inflation, non-fiscal conclusion, and carries forward the same real boundary condition (Raskin's neutral-rate upper bound) rather than inventing or swapping a different invalidation.
